summary.conclusion: The offline audit covered all OWASP Top 10 (2021) categories and verified authorization, kind-scoped and atomic state transitions, bounded tri-state parsing, immutable checkout, alarm gates, logging redaction, and fail-safe behavior. One major CWE-598 issue remains: the Telegraph credential is placed in the effective request URL; there are no critical findings, so the contract status is approved, but remediation is required. No Python dependencies were introduced; dependency review was limited to local manifests and diffs plus action-pin provenance, and no online CVE database was queried.

findings.title: Telegraph access token is sent in the request URL
findings.description: The fetch step combines curl's --get option with an access-token field read from a private file descriptor. The descriptor keeps the value out of the process argument list, but --get still serializes that field into the effective HTTPS URL query string, contrary to the Task 7 secret-isolation contract.
findings.impact: The credential can be retained by upstream, proxy, or diagnostic URL logging and could then be used for unauthorized Telegraph API operations under the configured account.
findings.recommendation: Remove --get and submit the token and limit as an HTTPS POST form body while retaining fetch-step-only environment ownership and file-descriptor input. Add a static workflow assertion that rejects query-string token transport, including the --get form used here.
findings.cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
